jessa (Docs): Heads-up: I'm updating the Optimize toolkit docs to reflect v2 behavior. Main asks: clarify prefetch default change, add a tiny SDK snippet, and fix an mkdocs redirect that 404s. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4360

ron (EngRT): Thanks. Do we have a recommended sentence for the prefetch change? I can paste into the PR.

jessa (Docs): One-liner: "Prefix KV prefetching is now opt-in in v2 to reduce memory pressure; enable when interactive latency matters." Will expand under migration notes.

nora (ML): Can we show a quick before/after for a common interactive config? e.g., batch=1, seq=1024. My numbers: v1 (prefetch on): 230 tok/s, v2 (prefetch off): 190 tok/s, v2 (prefetch on): 220 tok/s.

kai (SDK): I'll add an inline example for the Python SDK so docs readers can run migrate and toggle prefetch. Proposed snippet: ```py
from redwood import Optimize
opt = Optimize()
# migrate and enable prefetch for interactive workloads
profile = opt.migrate_quant_profile('/tmp/profile_v1.json')
profile['cache']['prefetch'] = True
opt.apply_profile(profile)
```

jessa (Docs): Nice. Keep it minimal. Also want a tiny YAML include showing the mkdocs redirect entry so the old /optimize/quant-profiles/v1 -> /optimize/quant-profiles. Can you add that, Ron?

ron (EngRT): On it. I'll add a redirect in mkdocs.yml and run linkcheck locally. Command: `make docs-linkcheck`

kai (SDK): I'll add a unit test asserting `tensor_type` exists after migrate and that `cache.prefetch` is present when set. Test name: `test_migrate_quant_profile_sets_tensor_type_and_prefetch`. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/992 (draft).

jessa (Docs): Also, small UX ask: can the SDK `migrate_quant_profile` return a tuple (profile, warnings) or include a `migration_warnings` key so we can surface to users in docs? If not, we'll show a note in docs.

kai (SDK): We can add a `migration_warnings` list in the returned dict. I'll include a short warning example: `['dtype renamed to tensor_type', 'prefetch default changed to false']`.

nora (ML): Add a short recommendation block: "Enable prefetch for single-user interactive apps; disable for high-throughput batched inference." Keeps guidance actionable.

preview-bot: Preview for PR 4360 deployed -> https://deploy-preview-4360--redwood-docs.netlify.app/optimize/v2-migration (expires in 7 days) :white_check_mark:

jessa (Docs): Preview looks mostly good. Two issues: code block for SDK lost line breaks in the generated page, and one anchor is still 404 (/optimize/quant-profiles/ref).

ron (EngRT): I fixed the anchor to /optimize/quant-profiles/reference and pushed `mkdocs.yml` redirect. Also changed the code fences to use ```py explicitly.

kai (SDK): Pushed tests and snippet to SDK PR. CI passed locally for unit tests. Linking files: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/992/files

jessa (Docs): Great. Leaving a small doc nit: use "schema update with automated conversion" instead of "breaking change" in the release notes. I'll add a short subsection "FAQ: common gotchas" with an item on `runtime.batch.max_delay_ms`.

nora (ML): One more micro-bench detail for the docs table: test harness 4xA100, batch sizes [1,4,16], seq=1024. Add the exact numbers in a tiny data row.

jessa (Docs): Will add a compact table and the SDK snippet. Plan to merge after the SDK PR merges and preview CI green. Targeting merge tomorrow AM and a short blurb in #announcements.

ron (EngRT): Linkcheck passed locally. No more 404s.

preview-bot: Docs CI passed for PR 4360 (mkdocs build + linkcheck).

jessa (Docs): Merging now. Follow-ups: add an examples repo script for bulk migrating many profiles, and a short on-prem note for quant profile differences. I'll file two issues.

kai (SDK): Thanks all. Filing issue for example script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/issues/210

jessa (Docs): Closing thread. Thanks everyone! :tada:
